---
title: "SSO Events by Application"
description: "Total SSO events for each application."
---

The total number of SSO events recorded for each application over a selected time
period.

IBM Verify raises an SSO event when someone who is already signed in reaches an
application. It uses the CanadaLogin session they already hold, so the person
enters no password and no second factor. This metric is useful for understanding usage
volume across CanadaLogin-integrated applications. It counts events, not people:
one person reaching an application several times contributes several events.

The source column is `total_logins`, but the event it counts is what IBM Verify
calls an SSO event, part of application usage.

## Calculation

Sum `total_logins` over the selected reporting period, grouped
by application.

**By service.** A service can have several applications, one per name IBM Verify
knows it by. To report a service, map each application to its service through
[`rp.alias`](../../catalog/rp/alias.qmd), then sum. SSO events are counts, so they
add up across a service's applications; unique users do not (see
[Cumulative Unique Users by Application](cumulative-unique-users-by-application.qmd)).
Keep an application with no `rp.alias` row under its own name rather than
dropping it, so the service totals still add up to the application totals.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

By application:

```sql
SELECT
  application_name,
  SUM(total_logins) AS total_sso_events
FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE  CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
-- optionally filter out internal applications; see the internal applications
-- note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND application_name NOT IN (
      SELECT al.alias
      FROM   rp.alias al
      JOIN   rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
      WHERE  s.is_internal
  )
GROUP  BY application_name
ORDER  BY total_sso_events DESC;
```

By service:

```sql
SELECT
  COALESCE(s.service_name_en, a.application_name) AS service,
  SUM(a.total_logins) AS total_sso_events
FROM   ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_app_login_counts a
-- left joins keep an application with no alias row, under its own name
LEFT JOIN rp.alias al ON a.application_name = al.alias
LEFT JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE  CAST(a.from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
  AND  NOT COALESCE(s.is_internal, FALSE)
-- aggregate after the join: several applications can map to one service
GROUP  BY COALESCE(s.service_name_en, a.application_name)
ORDER  BY total_sso_events DESC;
```

## R

By application:

```r
internal_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(is_internal) |>
  select(application_name = alias)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28")
  ) |>
  # optionally filter out internal applications; see the internal applications
  # note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  anti_join(internal_apps, by = "application_name") |>
  group_by(application_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_sso_events = sum(total_logins, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_sso_events))
```

By service:

```r
services <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  select(application_name = alias, service_name_en, is_internal)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28")
  ) |>
  # a left join keeps an application with no alias row, under its own name
  left_join(services, by = "application_name") |>
  filter(!coalesce(is_internal, FALSE)) |>
  # aggregate after the join: several applications can map to one service
  mutate(service = coalesce(service_name_en, application_name)) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  summarise(
    total_sso_events = sum(total_logins, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_sso_events))
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

This counts events, not people. Use this metric when the
question is about system usage or activity volume. Use unique user metrics when
the question is about reach.

These are a different IBM Verify event type from the CanadaLogin-wide
[authentication events](sign-ins.qmd), so never add the two together or
present them side by side as comparable figures. Unlike the authentication
events, SSO events are not inflated by second factors, because reaching an
application uses the session the person already holds rather than asking them
to authenticate again.

## Alternative names

- application usage
- SSO event volume
- single sign-on events
- total uses of CanadaLogin by application
- SSO events by service
